name: warp_register_row_reduction_sm120a
hypothesis: For RTX 5060 Laptop sm_120, assigning one block per RMSNorm row and keeping the partial sum in registers should reduce synchronization and shared-memory traffic versus a more general reduction. A two-level warp-shuffle reduction with only one shared value per warp, followed by a fused normalization/write pass, should improve geometric throughput while preserving the established warp-reduction direction from Episode 3.
changes: Use register-resident strided accumulation for each thread.
Reduce partial sums with warp shuffle instructions and a small shared warp-sum array.
Fuse inverse-RMS computation and weighted output in one CUDA launch.
Compile for CUDA sm_120a with Windows-compatible flags only.
constraints: No benchmark or CUDA execution performed.
